_comment: HTTP request model -- feature 29 (OWNER-DECISIONS.md Batch 1, feature doc
features/029-request.md, REQ-DEC-01 required + REQ-DEC-02).
REQ-DEC-01 (THE call, security + breaking): request.params is now
ROUTE-ONLY in all four -- a client's query/body value can never enter
params (REQ-PARAM-POLLUTION). Python's params was query+route merged
(route won on a same-name collision, but any OTHER client-controlled
query key rode along in params under a route-derived-looking
namespace); Ruby's params was query+BODY+route merged (same pollution,
plus a body leak); PHP/Node were already route-only (the reference).
BREAKING for Python/Ruby apps that read a query/body value via params.
The route-param accessor NAME is unified to `params` (py/php/node
already used it; Ruby renamed path_params -> params, deleting the old
merged params/build_params outright -- no back-compat alias). The
malformed-body result is pinned to the 3-of-4 majority (Python/PHP/Node
already agreed): a malformed JSON body -> the RAW STRING (Ruby changed
from {} via json_body's own always-a-Hash convenience method, which
keeps its documented contract unchanged for direct callers -- only the
parity-facing request.body path changed). The no-body sentinel is
pinned to each language's OWN native absence-value (None/null/nil/
undefined), checked BEFORE any content-type-specific parsing, matching
the pattern Python/PHP already had (Ruby's parse_body now returns nil
for an empty raw body instead of {}, and #body's own memoisation moved
off `||=` to a computed-flag, because nil is now a legitimate result).
REQ-DEC-02 (ratified by derivation from this same ledger's own stated
method -- majority-of-four / 'the reference' / RFC 7230 standard --
consistent with how Batch 4 of this ledger settled several other
either/or filter defaults by explicit 3-of-4-majority reasoning):
Python gains a mutable `user` field (REQ-PY-NO-USER) -- added to
__slots__, set by the secure-by-default auth gate AND by the (until now
silently broken) opt-in AuthMiddleware.before_request, which assigned
the nonexistent request.auth and raised AttributeError on every
SUCCESSFUL authentication against the real Request class (only its own
mock-based test hid this -- fixed here, no-mock, alongside the field).
Immutability (REQ-IMMUTABILITY-DIVERGE) is reconciled to the PHP
`readonly` / Ruby writer-less-attr_reader reference (both ALREADY
correct, no change): Python blocks reassignment of the 14 core
wire-derived fields once from_scope() completes (__setattr__ guard,
params/session/user/_-prefixed fields stay writable); Node marks the 8
matching TS interface fields `readonly` (compile-time; a Writable<T>
local view lets createRequest() still build them once). The header()
dash rule (REQ-HEADER-DASH-DIVERGE) is reconciled to the PHP/Node
reference (case-fold only, matching RFC 7230 3.2 -- no `-`/`_`
substitution): Python drops its `-`->`_` remap, Ruby drops its `_`->`-`
remap. Ruby's Rack multipart dependency (REQ-RUBY-RACK-DEP) is NOTED,
not changed -- Ruby's own HTTP server IS Rack, so this is not an extra
runtime dependency the way it would be for a language with no Rack in
its request path; hand-rolling multipart would be a net LOSS against
the maintainability-means-less-code principle for zero real benefit.
DO NOT REGRESS: client-IP trust was already PARITY (a strength) --
remote_ip is always the raw socket peer (never X-Forwarded-For); ip
honours X-Forwarded-For ONLY when the peer is a configured
TINA4_TRUSTED_PROXIES entry (empty/unset = trust nothing), same
rightmost-non-trusted-hop algorithm in all four. The algorithm itself
is UNCHANGED by this feature -- ip-honours-xff-only-from-trusted-proxy
locks it under the shared fixture name; the deeper per-language suites
(test_trusted_proxy.py / TrustedProxyTest.php / trusted_proxy_spec.rb /
trustedProxy.test.ts) are untouched and still the primary coverage.
NO MOCKS. Every case drives a REAL registered route through the REAL
front controller/dispatch (TestClient in all four, backed by
Router.dispatch in PHP, RackApp#call in Ruby, core.server.app in
Python, Router.match+enforceRouteAuth in Node) or, where TestClient
cannot control the socket peer, a real ASGI app dispatch (Python) / a
real Request constructed with an explicit remoteIp then
Router::dispatch (PHP) / a real Rack env with REMOTE_ADDR then
RackApp#call (Ruby) / a REAL node:http server + a real loopback TCP
connection (Node, matching test/trustedProxy.test.ts's own
gold-standard pattern) for the IP-trust case.
Mutation-proved (Python, Ruby -- the two languages REQ-PARAM-POLLUTION
actually changed; PHP/Node were never vulnerable, so there is nothing to
mutate there): reinstating the query-seeded-then-route-merged `params`
construction (Python: `req.params = dict(req.query)` in from_scope() +
`self.params.update(...)` instead of overwrite in the route-attach step;
Ruby: re-adding a `query.each { |k,v| result[k]=v }` line before the
path-params loop in the `params` getter) turns
route_param_not_shadowed_by_query RED in both -- the unrelated `extra`
query key leaks into `params`, which is exactly the pollution surface
this feature closes. Restored after in both.
Each invariant names a REAL suite file per framework carrying the SAME
case names in each language's own idiom, which
scripts/audit-contract-fixtures.py normalises and matches.
feature: 29 - HTTP request model (REQ-DEC-01 required: params route-only in all four + unified route-param name `params` + pinned malformed/empty-body result; REQ-DEC-02: Python request.user + immutability posture (PHP/Ruby already correct, Python/Node now match) + header() dash rule reconciled to PHP/Node + Ruby Rack multipart noted not changed)

invariants.rule: request.params is ROUTE-ONLY in all four -- a client query-string value can never enter it, under its own name or any other. A route `/{id}` hit as `/{route-id}?id={other}&extra=leak` yields params["id"] == the ROUTE value, query["id"] == the client value, and "extra" (a client-only key with no route counterpart) never appears in params at all. Identical in all four (Python request.params/request.query; PHP $request->params/$request->query; Ruby request.params/request.query; Node req.params/req.query).
invariants.why: REQ-PARAM-POLLUTION (the security finding): Python's params used to be query+route merged (route won a same-name collision, but ANY other client-controlled query key rode along in params too -- a handler trusting request.params["admin"] as route-derived data could actually be reading an attacker-supplied query value for a key that happens to have no route segment at all); Ruby's params merged query+BODY+route the same way. PHP/Node were already route-only (the reference this release aligns Python/Ruby to). Mutation-proved on Python and Ruby: reinstating the old query-seeded-then-merged construction turns this RED (the `extra` key leaks into params); restored after.

invariants.rule: A malformed (unparseable) JSON body with Content-Type: application/json yields the RAW STRING (the unparsed body bytes, decoded as text) as request.body, in all four -- pinned to the Python/PHP/Node majority. Ruby changed from returning {} (an empty Hash indistinguishable from a genuinely-empty valid JSON object) to the raw string; Ruby's separate json_body convenience method (Hash-only, {} on failure, not part of this parity contract) is unchanged for its own direct callers.
invariants.why: REQ-BODY-DIVERGE: before this release a handler that decoded a bad body saw a STRING in three languages and an EMPTY HASH in Ruby -- silently indistinguishable from `{}` sent as valid JSON, so a malformed-body bug could pass Ruby-only testing unnoticed. Pinning to the 3-of-4 majority is the same tie-break method this ledger already used elsewhere (OWNER-DECISIONS.md Batch 4, `|join`/`|default` filter defaults, '3-of-4 majority').

invariants.rule: The secure-by-default auth gate stashes the verified JWT payload on request.user (mutable), and a route handler behind that gate reads the same claims back. Identical field name and shape in all four (Python request.user; PHP $request->user; Ruby request.user; Node req.user).
invariants.why: REQ-PY-NO-USER: Python's Request had no `user` attribute at all, and __slots__ actively BLOCKED a handler or middleware from setting one -- PHP/Ruby/Node already exposed it. Python's own opt-in AuthMiddleware.before_request tried to set the (never-declared) request.auth and raised AttributeError on every successful authentication against the real Request class; its only test used a hand-rolled mock with no __slots__, which silently accepted the assignment and hid the break entirely (fixed here, no-mock, alongside adding the field). PHP/Ruby/Node were already correct -- locked in here under the shared fixture name, not re-fixed.

invariants.rule: request.remote_ip is ALWAYS the raw socket peer, never X-Forwarded-For. request.ip honours X-Forwarded-For ONLY when the raw peer is listed in TINA4_TRUSTED_PROXIES (empty/unset = trust nothing); otherwise ip == remote_ip regardless of any forwarding header the client sends. Identical rightmost-non-trusted-hop algorithm in all four -- this feature does not touch it, only locks it under the shared fixture name.
invariants.why: Already measured PARITY (a strength) in the feature-29 audit -- included here so the new shared fixture carries a positive proof of the one property that was already correct, not just the three that changed, and so a future regression on ANY of the four is caught by the SAME fixture the breaking param-pollution fix lives in.
